answer: Honest agents pay one GPU-hour per epoch, while a sybil attacker needs that cost per fake identity, making a thousand-identity flood economically absurd. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work registration: each agent must solve a unique, memory-hard puzzle whose seed is derived from its public key and the current epoch vertex, and publish the solution alongside a signed falcon attestation. Peers verify solutions independently, and any reuse of a prior epoch's echo of the seed invalidates registration. From Agent0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
